what: Social Media Image Resizer turns one photo, or many, into the right size for each platform in one go: Instagram posts, stories, reel covers and profile pictures, TikTok covers, YouTube thumbnails and banners, Facebook posts, covers and event images, X posts and headers, LinkedIn posts and banners, Pinterest pins and WhatsApp profile pictures and status.

Tick the sizes you need. In "Fill the frame" mode you drag a focus point onto the important part of the photo so every crop keeps it in view. In "Show the whole photo" mode nothing is cut and the gaps get a blurred or coloured background.
Everything runs in your browser, so your photos are not uploaded. The tool is not affiliated with any of these platforms; sizes are the commonly recommended ones and platforms may change them.
uses: Make every size for one announcement image at once.
Tick "All profile pictures" and get one file for each platform.
Create a YouTube banner, Facebook cover, X header and LinkedIn banner from one photo.
Make 9:16 versions for Instagram, TikTok and WhatsApp in one click.
Resize a batch of photos for several clients or platforms and download one ZIP.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop photos here" or drop one or more photos. Tap a thumbnail to work on that photo, or its × to remove it.
Under "Sizes to make", tick each size you need. The quick buttons "All profile pictures" and "All 9:16 stories" tick a whole set; "Clear selection" unticks everything.

In "Fit" choose "Fill the frame (crop to fit)" for full-bleed images or "Show the whole photo (add background)" to avoid any cropping. For the second, choose a blurred, solid colour or white background.
In fill mode, drag the dot (or tap) onto the most important part of the photo, such as a face. Every crop keeps it in view. Each photo has its own focus point.
Small previews show every selected size. Profile pictures show the circle they are displayed in, and the YouTube banner shows the safe area that is visible on every device.
Choose JPG or PNG in "Download as" and click "Download". With more than one image you get a ZIP with files named like photo-instagram-story-1080x1920.jpg.
features: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest and WhatsApp.
Tick as many sizes as you like and get them all together.
Resize several photos to every chosen size in one ZIP.
Drag a dot to keep faces and products in every crop.
Fit the whole photo with a blurred, colour or white background.
Circle preview for profile pictures and a safe area for YouTube banners.
Each file name says the platform, use and pixel size.

example.title: Worked example: one photo for every profile
example.text: Priya has a 2400 × 3000 headshot. She clicks "All profile pictures", leaves "Fit" on "Fill the frame" and drags the focus dot onto her face. The previews show her face centred in each circle. She clicks "Download 7 images as ZIP" and gets files such as headshot-linkedin-profile-picture-400x400.jpg and headshot-youtube-profile-picture-800x800.jpg.

tips: Start from the largest, sharpest photo you have; downsizing keeps it crisp, enlarging makes it soft.
For banners, keep text and faces inside the middle of the image, because apps crop the edges differently on phones and computers.
Use PNG for graphics with text or logos and JPG for photos.
Profile pictures are shown as circles, so keep the face in the centre with some space around it.
Platforms update their recommended sizes now and then. If an upload is cropped unexpectedly, check the platform's current help page.
problems: A face is cut off in one size
Drag the focus dot onto the face. Very wide sizes like headers show only a thin strip of a tall photo, so choose "Show the whole photo" if you need everything.
The preview says the photo will look soft
Your photo is smaller than that size. Use a bigger original if you have one.
Only image files can be resized. Convert HEIC photos to JPG first.
Click the "Save …" button that appears next to "Download"; some browsers block automatic downloads.
